item.content:encoded:
Defence and International Security

发布源: 36. Casimir Pulaski Foundation --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-07-22

The Pulaski Foundation Defence and Security Program provides multidisciplinary analysis of the current and emerging defense and security challenges facing the Transatlantic Alliance – with a special focus on Central and Eastern Europe.

Since 2022 the program allocates much of its resources to analysing the possible outcomes and consequences for European security of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. A special component of the program is devoted to the challenges and opportunities facing Poland’s defense policy, including modernizing of the Polish army and its industry. The main goal is to present actionable recommendations to an array of Polish stakeholders, including public administration, which could form a basis for long-term strategies for Poland in times of raising military and defense demands.

Overall, through its analysis, the program advocates for a stronger presence of NATO on the Alliance’s Eastern Flank, more developed European defence capabilities and argues for the need to provide military assistance and solid security guarantees to Ukraine.

item.content:encoded:
Latvia: significant increase in migratory pressure from Belarus

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-07-22

On 13 July, Lithuania’s Minister of the Interior, Martynas Katelynas, proposed the introduction of temporary controls at the border with Latvia in response to a significant increase in the number of migrants entering Lithuania from Belarus through Latvian territory. Data from the Lithuanian Ministry of the Interior indicate that secondary migration from Latvia increased fourfold in the first six months of this year compared to the same period last year, rising from approximately 300 to 1,200 cases. Katelynas noted that potential measures could replicate those implemented by Poland at its border with Lithuania, specifically the reintroduction of temporary border controls. He emphasised, however, that such strict measures would be considered if the volume of illegal border crossings exceeded the capacity of Lithuania’s border services. Both the president and prime minister of Lithuania have expressed opposition to the implementation of these controls.

Migratory pressure from Belarus at the Latvia–Belarus border has continued to increase steadily. In 2025, the authorities prevented 12,046 illegal border crossing attempts. By mid-July 2026, approximately 8,000 such incidents had been recorded. The number of attempted crossings rises significantly during the summer months, with around 1,000 attempts prevented in the first two weeks of July alone. Ukraine: new government overshadowed by a controversial dismissal

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-07-22

On 16 July, the Verkhovna Rada approved Serhii Koretskyi as prime minister by a majority of 289 votes and confirmed the composition of his cabinet. The new government reversed the merger of two ‘super-ministries’. The Ministry of Economy, Environment and Agricultural Policy was split into the Ministry of Economy, headed by Oleksandr Kravchenko, and the Ministry of Agrarian Policy, led by Taras Vysotskyi. The outgoing minister, Oleksii Soboliev, is expected to become deputy head of the Presidential Office for Economic Affairs. The Ministry for Development of Communities and Territories was also divided into two separate ministries: the Ministry of Reconstruction, Infrastructure and Transport, headed by Mykola Kalashnyk, and the Ministry of Communities, Territories, and Internally Displaced Persons, led by Vitalii Bezhin. Other notable changes include Vsevolod Chentsov replacing Taras Kachka as Deputy Prime Minister for European and Euro-Atlantic Integration, and Ivan Vyhivskyi succeeding Ihor Klymenko as Minister of Internal Affairs (see Appendices 1 and 2).

Several senior ministers retained their positions, including First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Energy Denys Shmyhal and Finance Minister Serhii Marchenko.
